newsitem.title: KENYA: Bad weather, insecurity hamper aid work in Zaire.
newsitem.headline: Bad weather, insecurity hamper aid work in Zaire.

text.p: The U.N. World Food Programme (WFP) said on Tuesday insecurity and bad weather would create new obstacles to feeding 170,000 Rwandan refugees in eastern Zaire, where rebels are battling government forces.
WFP said the growing problem of heavy cloud cover with the onset of the rainy season would limit flights to refugee camps such as Tingi Tingi and road routes would be impassable because of rain.

"It is ironic that in a moment when we have overcome many complex problems affecting food deliveries, other uncontrollable constraints and insecurity are threatening to curb our operation," said WFP spokesman Trevor Rower in a statement.

"Relief operations to eastern Zaire continue to be hampered by tremendous logistical constraints," he added. "Impassable roads, small airstrips, scarce fuel supplies and insecurity are still major hurdles."

WFP on Monday ended distributing a seven-day food package to the 170,000 Rwandan refugees at Tingi Tingi. It said ample food stocks there would be bolstered by more convoys from Kisangani on Wednesday.
